Rina (APAC Eng): Quick flag — Lunar New Year observed day moved this year from 02/10 to 02/11 in our Singapore calendar, but people booked PTO on 02/11 and the system also granted the observed holiday on 02/11. A few folks got double-deducted. @people-ops? :worried:
Jordan (People Ops): Thanks for flagging. Can you paste the affected IDs here or DM me? We need manager approval to reverse per audit.
Rina (APAC Eng): Pasting sanitized list: eid:51001 Mei L., eid:51002 Jun P., eid:51003 Arif H. All booked 2027-02-11 as personal PTO but office observance moved to 02/11 so they ended up losing a day.
Ken (Payroll): Looping payroll — looks like the locale calendar sync applied the new observed date but didn't exclude existing PTO bookings. We can run a reversal if manager confirms. Command I'll run once approved: python payroll/scripts/fix_observed_overlap.py --ids 51001,51002,51003 --region SG --note "lunar2027-observed-overlap"
Mai (Manager): I confirm and approve reversals for those three employees. Please proceed and attach this approval to the audit ticket.
Ken (Payroll): Reversal queued and applied; AJ-2027-211 created. Updated HRIS balances and added detection rule HR_HOL_045 to flag booking vs observed-date overlaps during calendar merges.
Jordan (People Ops): I'll add a short FAQ and update the time-off policy: when an observed holiday shifts, we will not auto-deduct already-booked PTO on that same date and managers can request a reversal with the approval chain. Filing incident HR-2027-112 for audit trail. Thanks everyone for the quick reports!
